question.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(y)=10{y}^{3}+5{y}^{2}-5y.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(y)=0,$ that is

$$
10{y}^{3}+5{y}^{2}-5y=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $5y.$ We can factor out the $5y$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y(2{y}^{2}+y-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{y}^{2}+y-1$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y(2{y}^{2}+y-1) & =0 \\ 5y(2y-1)(y+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $y=0,$ $y=\frac{1}{2},$ and $y=-1$
